directAnswer: You can free up storage on your phone by deleting unused apps, clearing cache, and transferring media files to cloud storage or an external device.
summary: Freeing up storage on your phone involves managing apps, media, and system files effectively.

sections.heading: Delete Unused Apps
sections.body: Go through your apps and uninstall any that you no longer use. This can significantly free up space.

sections.heading: Clear Cache
sections.body: Apps often store temporary files that can accumulate over time. Clearing the cache can help recover storage without losing important data.

sections.heading: Transfer Media Files
sections.body: Consider moving photos, videos, and music to cloud storage services or an external hard drive to free up local storage.

steps.title: Delete Unused Apps (Android)
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Apps > Select the app > Uninstall.

steps.title: Delete Unused Apps (iOS)
steps.detail: Press and hold the app icon until it jiggles, then tap the 'X' to delete.

steps.title: Clear App Cache (Android)
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Storage > Cached data > Clear cached data.

steps.title: Transfer Media Files
steps.detail: Use cloud services like Google Drive or iCloud to upload your media files.

faqs.question: Will deleting apps affect my data?
faqs.answer: If you delete an app, you may lose data associated with it unless it's backed up.

faqs.question: How do I know which apps take up the most space?
faqs.answer: You can check storage usage in Settings > Storage to see which apps are using the most space.

faqs.question: Is it safe to clear cache?
faqs.answer: Yes, clearing cache is generally safe and can help improve app performance.

caveats: Some apps may need to be reconfigured after clearing cache or uninstalling.
